# CLI usage

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask docs`. Do not edit. -->

Global connection values resolve in this order: command flags, environment variables, then the selected context.

## `dokploy`

```text
Manage Dokploy resources from the command line

Usage: dokploy [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  init         Create a starter declarative configuration
  schema       Print the declarative configuration JSON Schema
  validate     Parse and validate a declarative configuration offline
  coverage     Show the effective resource specification and API coverage ledger
  fmt          Rewrite declarative documents in canonical form
  doctor       Check the connection, Dokploy version, access, organization, and selector catalogs
  completions  Generate a shell completion script on standard output
  plan         Compare configuration, durable state, and fresh Dokploy state without mutating anything
  apply        Preview and reconcile configuration against fresh Dokploy state
  deploy       Deploy converged applications, Compose services, and databases
  recover      Reconcile an interrupted apply from durable journal evidence
  destroy      Delete every resource tracked by this workspace from Dokploy
  state        Inspect resources tracked in the local workspace state
  context      Inspect or select local connection contexts
  import       Adopt existing Dokploy resources into a new declarative workspace
  api          Call one operation from the pinned Dokploy API contract directly
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --url <URL>
          Override the Dokploy base URL

      --api-key <KEY>
          Override the Dokploy API key

      --allow-unsupported-version
          Permit mutations against a Dokploy version outside the supported set

  -h, --help
          Print help

  -V, --version
          Print version
```

## `dokploy init`

```text
Create a starter declarative configuration

Usage: dokploy init [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --file <PATH>
          Configuration file to create. Defaults to `dokploy.yaml`, or to `dokploy.settings.yaml` with `--settings`

      --url <URL>
          Override the Dokploy base URL

      --api-key <KEY>
          Override the Dokploy API key

      --empty
          Create the canonical empty configuration without prompting

      --allow-unsupported-version
          Permit mutations against a Dokploy version outside the supported set

      --settings
          Create an instance settings document instead of a project document

  -h, --help
          Print help

  -V, --version
          Print version
```

## `dokploy schema`

```text
Print the declarative configuration JSON Schema

Usage: dokploy schema [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --document <DOCUMENT>
          Which document the schema describes

          Possible values:
          - project:  A `project:` document
          - settings: A `settings:` document
          
          [default: project]

      --url <URL>
          Override the Dokploy base URL

      --api-key <KEY>
          Override the Dokploy API key

      --allow-unsupported-version
          Permit mutations against a Dokploy version outside the supported set

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version
```

## `dokploy plan`

```text
Compare configuration, durable state, and fresh Dokploy state without mutating anything

Usage: dokploy plan [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --file <PATH>
          Plan one explicit document instead of the workspace manifest

      --url <URL>
          Override the Dokploy base URL

      --all
          Plan the workspace manifest. Kept as an explicit compatibility alias

      --api-key <KEY>
          Override the Dokploy API key

      --allow-unsupported-version
          Permit mutations against a Dokploy version outside the supported set

      --json
          Print the deterministic redaction-safe JSON plan

      --detailed-exitcode
          Return status 2 when a complete, applyable plan contains changes

  -h, --help
          Print help

  -V, --version
          Print version
```

## `dokploy apply`

```text
Preview and reconcile configuration against fresh Dokploy state

Usage: dokploy apply [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --file <PATH>
          Apply one explicit document instead of the workspace manifest

      --url <URL>
          Override the Dokploy base URL

      --all
          Apply the workspace manifest. Kept as an explicit compatibility alias

      --api-key <KEY>
          Override the Dokploy API key

      --allow-unsupported-version
          Permit mutations against a Dokploy version outside the supported set

      --auto-approve
          Apply a complete plan without interactive confirmation

      --allow-disruptive
          Permit disruptive changes during a non-interactive apply

      --deploy
          Deploy eligible resources after configuration converges

  -h, --help
          Print help

  -V, --version
          Print version
```

## `dokploy deploy`

```text
Deploy converged applications, Compose services, and databases

Usage: dokploy deploy [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --file <PATH>
          Deploy resources from one explicit document instead of the workspace manifest

      --url <URL>
          Override the Dokploy base URL

      --all
          Deploy the workspace manifest. Kept as an explicit compatibility alias

      --api-key <KEY>
          Override the Dokploy API key

      --allow-unsupported-version
          Permit mutations against a Dokploy version outside the supported set

      --target <ADDR>
          Force one resource selected by its full address or unique suffix. Repeatable

      --wait
          Wait for queued application and Compose deployments to finish

      --no-wait
          Return after Dokploy accepts queued deployments

      --timeout <TIMEOUT>
          Maximum wait for each asynchronous deployment (`30s`, `20m`, `2h`)
          
          [default: 20m]

      --parallelism <PARALLELISM>
          Maximum independent deployments to run at once
          
          [default: 4]

      --auto-approve
          Deploy without interactive confirmation

  -h, --help
          Print help

  -V, --version
          Print version
```

## `dokploy state`

```text
Inspect resources tracked in the local workspace state

Usage: dokploy state [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  list       List tracked logical resource addresses
  show       Show one tracked resource without exposing managed values or receipts
  mv         Move one tracked logical address without changing Dokploy
  rm         Stop tracking one resource without deleting it from Dokploy
  protect    Prevent declarative deletion of one tracked resource
  unprotect  Allow declarative deletion of one tracked resource
  help       Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --file <PATH>
          Configuration file whose directory owns the state
          
          [default: dokploy.yaml]

      --url <URL>
          Override the Dokploy base URL

      --api-key <KEY>
          Override the Dokploy API key

      --allow-unsupported-version
          Permit mutations against a Dokploy version outside the supported set

  -h, --help
          Print help

  -V, --version
          Print version
```
